'''Joshua Evan Greene''' (born in 1981) is a mathematician whose primary area of research is [[low-dimensional topology]]. He is a professor at [[Boston College]].  Greene solved the lens space realization problem, while he and a co-author have made advances in the understanding of the [[inscribed square problem]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IQqtsm-bBRU |title=This open problem taught me what topology is |website=youtube.com |date=24 December 2024 }}</ref>

==Education and career==
Greene completed his undergraduate studies at [[Harvey Mudd College]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hmc.edu/about/2022/11/07/joshua-greene-02-to-receive-2023-levi-l-conant-prize/|title=Joshua Greene '02 to Receive 2023 Levi L. Conant Prize|website=www.hmc.edu|language=en}}</ref> and at the [[University of Chicago]].  He received his PhD in mathematics from [[Princeton University]] in 2009,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alum Joshua Greene *09 to Receive 2023 Conant Prize |url=https://www.math.princeton.edu/news/alumn-joshua-greene-09-receive-2023-conant-prize |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=www.math.princeton.edu}}</ref> with [[Zoltán Szabó (mathematician)|Zoltán Szabó]] as advisor (thesis: ''Donaldson's Theorem, Heegaard Floer Homology, and Results on Knots'').<ref>{{Cite web |title=Joshua Greene - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=134698 |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref>

After completing his doctoral degree, Greene worked as a [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] Postdoctoral Fellow from 2009 to 2011 at [[Columbia University]]. Greene is currently a professor at [[Boston College]].<ref name="quanta">Kevin Hartnett (June 25, 2020), "New Geometric Perspective Cracks Old Problem About Rectangles" (''[[Quanta Magazine]]'') https://www.quantamagazine.org/new-geometric-perspective-cracks-old-problem-about-rectangles-20200625/</ref>

==Mathematical work==
In early work, Greene solved the lens space realization problem for knot surgery.<ref>{{Cite web | title=The lens space realization problem|url=https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v177-n2-p03-p.pdf |website=annals.math.princeton.edu| language=en}}</ref>

In 2020, together with Andrew Lobb, Greene [[Mathematical proof|proved]] the rectangular peg [[conjecture]].<ref name="quanta" /><ref name="notices">{{Cite web | title=A survey on the square peg problem|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201404/rnoti-p346.pdf |website=www.ams.org| language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=The rectangular peg problem |date=2021 |url=https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2021/194-2/p04|website=annals.math.princeton.edu| language=en}}</ref>  Later they resolved the cyclic quadrilateral peg problem<ref name="notices" /><ref>{{Cite web | title=What's Happening in the Mathematical Sciences, volume 12|url=https://bookstore.ams.org/happening-12?_gl=1*5qn521*_ga*Nzk3MjM0MjE1LjE2OTcyMTIwNDg.*_ga_26G4XFTR63*czE3NTA0MzI3MTQkbzE2JGcxJHQxNzUwNDMyNzY2JGo4JGwwJGgw&_ga=2.269061937.1323241771.1750432715-797234215.1697212048 |website=bookstore.ams.org| language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Greene |first1=Joshua Evan |last2=Lobb |first2=Andrew | title=Cyclic quadrilaterals and smooth Jordan curves |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00222-023-01212-6 |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|date=2023 |volume=234 |issue=3 |pages=931–935 |doi=10.1007/s00222-023-01212-6 |arxiv=2011.05216 |bibcode=2023InMat.234..931G |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Greene was awarded the 2002 [[Morgan Prize]] for his simple topological proof of [[Kneser graph#Chromatic number|Kneser's conjecture]].  He received the [[Levi L. Conant Prize]] in 2023 for his article in the [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]].  His work was featured in the 2021 Current Events Bulletin of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/meetings/lectures/2021-web-master-ceb.pdf |website=www.ams.org | title=Current Events Bulletin of the AMS 2021}}</ref>  He was a 2024 Simons Fellow in mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2024/03/20/2024-simons-fellows-in-mathematics-announced |website=www.simonsfoundation.org|title=2024 Simons Fellows in Mathematics}}</ref>  Together with Andrew Lobb, in 2025 Greene won a Frontiers of Science Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.icbs.cn/site/pages/index/index?pageId=0c7b3697-53db-42b4-a419-40338eda7ccd |website=www.icbs.cn | title=The Frontiers of Science Award 2025}}</ref> for their work resolving the rectangular peg problem.
